Red Hat Enterprise Linux System Administration I | Study

This chapter shows you how to move command output into files and into other commands. You also learn to edit text files with the Vim editor. Last, you learn to use shell variables to change how your shell and your programs behave.

Editing Text Files from the Shell Prompt
Vim is a text editor that works in a text-only terminal and is almost always on a server.
Linux keeps most settings in plain text files, so any text editor can change them. Vim is an improved version of the older
standard (a set of rules Linux follows), so a server with any editor nearly always has Vim. It also works over
(a way to log in to another computer) with no desktop needed.
Learn Vim because it is almost always there when you log in remotely.
